name: Thoracic Outlet Arterial Syndrome
definition: Arterial compression at the thoracic outlet, often associated with a cervical rib, causing ischemia, aneurysm or embolic complications.

investigations.principle: CTA/MRA and vascular ultrasound characterize compression and arterial complications.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, marrow, vascular, occult injury or other condition-specific assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific imaging pathway.

green: Urgent vascular referral for ischemic disease
amber: Definitive treatment often requires decompression with arterial repair when structural injury exists.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Rakta-vaha vascular phenotype may be documented only in parallel.

patientEducation.summary: Arterial compression at the thoracic outlet, often associated with a cervical rib, causing ischemia, aneurysm or embolic complications.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe vascular symptoms, infection/systemic illness, major trauma, sphincter change or other listed red flags.
